Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin Day 3 finally! The West Indies players make their way out to the middle, followed by Dean Elgar and Aiden Markram. Kemar Roach will start with the ball.

Update 1200 local (1600 GMT) - We have news that the inspection is going on and the sun is shining. We are also hearing that play will resume at 1240 local (1640 GMT). This is very good news and let's hope that the rain stays away. Stay with us.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

UPDATE 1132 local time (1532 GMT) The umpires have decided to call off the first session. It's time for Lunch now. Further inspection is scheduled for 1150 local time. Hopefully, the umpires give a thumbs up for the remaining sessions. Stay tuned for more updates.

UPDATE 1052 local (1452 GMT)  The umpires did a complete inspection and it looks like there are some wet patches at the outfield. There will be another inspection in about 30 minutes at 11.20 am local time. Hope we get a better news this time. Stay tuned for more updates.
UPDATE 1020 local (1420 GMT) In some news, inspection to be held at 10.45 am local, just about 25 minutes from now. Let's hope that we hear some good news then.

PITCH REPORT- Mike Haysman says that the pitch has settled down a bit. States that the color of the pitch has changed a bit too. Sir Curtly Ambrose adds that the pitch is much greener but it should be easier for batting now.
PITCH REPORT- Mike Haysmen says that the pitch has settled down a bit. Sir Curtly Ambrose adds that the pitch is much greener and the batters would like to take advantage of it.

UPDATE 0942 local (1342 GMT) Not the news you want to hear. But the rain has started to pour at the Darren Sammy Cricket Ground, St Lucia. The covers are also on. We might have a delayed start. Let's keep our fingers crossed and hope we get some action soon.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 3 of the Test match between West Indies and South Africa. On Day 2, the South Africans thoroughly dominated the whole day. As they rattled out the West Indies side within two sessions of play. The West Indies are currently trailing by 149 runs. The visitors have a strong lead already and will look to put on a huge total on the board. Meanwhile, the key for West Indies will be to get early breakthroughs. A very exciting day of Test cricket awaits us. Stay with us for further updates.
...Day 3, Session 1...

South African have a big lead now of 149. They would look to drive home the advantage by batting well on Day 3. Windies will need wickets and that too really quickly. Will they get it? Will there be a fightback? We will find out. Do join us for the action. Till then, take care and goodbye!

Wiaan Mulder was the tormentor in chief as he got three wickets in the last session. However, it has been a complete team effort from the visitors as every bowler took a wicket at least. Dean Elgar will be pretty pleased with his side.

It seemed like the Windies would continue their batting on Day 3 but once Joshua Da Silva fell, it happened all quickly. The lower-order failed to show any resistance and Jermaine Blackwood in the end, lost his wicket as he looked to get to his fifty.

Another poor batting performance from the Windies! They have really struggled against this South African attack. They kept losing wickets in regular intervals and lost way too many towards the end of the day.

OUT! Caught! Blackwood falls one short of a half ton. That is also the end of the Windies innings. He was looking to get to his fifty with a big shot. It is on middle, Blackwood looks to play the slog sweep but he gets a top edge and Elgar at covers takes a good catch. WINDIES BOWLED OUT FOR 149!
Commentary.Howout: c Dean Elgar b Keshav Maharaj

... Day 2, Session 3 ...

Windies need a partnership. Hope is set and Blackwood needs to hang in there. They are another 242 runs away and if they do not get a partnership, it's going to be tough for them to get back into the game. More of the same is what South Africa will want. Will we see a fightback?

4 bowlers bowled for the visitors in this session and all got a wicket at least. It was Rabada who started things off as he dismissed Brathwaite on the very first ball. Powell and Chase did not last long. Mayers and Hope did start to build a stand but Maharaj then got the breakthrough.

South Africa tired their best to sneak in another over. Maharaj was all set and had his cap off but the umpire's push the bails off and they walk off for Tea. Don't blame the visitors to try and bowl one more, this has been an outstanding session for them.
